words.meaning: An email or web page that pretends to be someone trusted, to steal passwords or money.
A second check when you sign in, like a code sent to your phone.
A private, locked connection to the work network over the internet.
To cut a device off from the network. It stays on but cannot reach other computers.
A network guard that lets data in or out based on a list of rules.
A harmful program that locks files and asks for money to unlock them.
To move a file into a locked area where it cannot run or spread.
A list of programs or sites that security tools let run or connect without stopping them.
A short code worked out from a file. The same file always gives the same code.
The security app on each computer. It watches for attacks and can cut the computer off the network.
Data loss prevention. A tool that watches for private data leaving the company.
The list of all company devices, with who owns them and where they are.
A middle point that all web visits pass through. It can allow or deny sites.
Penetration test. Testers the company pays try to break in, to find weak spots.
A step-by-step guide for handling one kind of security event.
The schedule of planned work on systems, with dates, times and owners.
A legal order to keep all records about a case. Nothing in it may be deleted.
Threat intelligence. Shared news about attackers, their tools and the signs they leave.
A command tool built into many work computers. It runs typed commands and small programs.
A tool to see and control a computer from far away.
A mailbox setting that acts on new mail by itself, like forwarding copies elsewhere.
Tests that show whether an email really came from the domain it names.
The name part of an email or web address, like example.com.
A person or login with extra power to install apps, change settings and manage accounts.
A record a system keeps of what happened and when.
